sections.title: Why Study Law in the UK?
sections.lead: Students interested in a career in legal practice, corporate law, international law, human rights or public service should consider Studying Law in the UK. The UK is internationally recognized for its long tradition of law practice, its universities and its legal education system which attracts students from all over the world.

groups.text: Main advantages of studying law in the UK

items: UK law degrees are recognized around the world and can be a passport to opportunities in legal practice, industry, government and academia.
A strong legal education gives students an understanding of legal systems, legislation, case law and legal reasoning and analytical thought.
Areas of specialization : Students can study subjects like international law, criminal law, corporate law, commercial law, human rights and intellectual property law .
Many programs include mooting, legal research, case analysis, negotiation exercises and legal clinics.
International Exposure: Students are exposed to legal issues that arise in world government, international business and trade.
Legal graduates are employed in legal firms, corporations, financial institutions, government agencies, non-profits and compliance departments.
Shorter study option: Most UK LLB degrees last for three years but some graduate-entry and accelerated programs may vary in length.
Students who have the right qualifications can follow professional qualification routes to become a solicitor or barrister in England and Wales.

sections.title: Law Courses in the UK
sections.lead: UK universities offer undergraduate, graduate and research law courses. The course which is better for a student depends on his/her past education, interests and career goals.

items: Famous Courses in Law
The Bachelor of Laws (LLB) is an undergraduate degree which covers the basic subjects of law and is a prerequisite to further legal education.
Some universities offer a law degree known as a "BA Law", which combines study of law with other academic disciplines.
If you already have a degree and want to study law, you can do a Graduate Entry LLB.
The Master of Laws, or LLM, is a postgraduate qualification that enables students to focus on a specific area of law.
LLM International Business law. The focus is on international business transactions, company regulation and cross-border legal issues.
LLM Corporate Law comprises company law, corporate governance, mergers and acquisitions and business regulation.
LLM International Law is the study of the principles of international law, treaties, international organizations and state to state relations.
LLM Human Rights Law covers human rights frameworks, legal protections, and international human rights issues.
LLM Criminal Law examines criminal justice, criminal responsibility and associated legal issues.
LLM Intellectual Property Copyright, Patents, Trademarks and Intellectual Property Protection Law.
Students who wish to do specialized policy work, pursue academic careers, or engage in advanced legal research should earn a PhD in law.
Duration of the Course
LLB programs in England, Wales and Northern Ireland are typically full-time and last three years.
Some fast-track or graduate-entry law degrees can be completed in a shorter period.
Most full-time LLM programs last one year.
The time it takes to complete a full-time PhD program depends on the university and research subject, but it's usually between three and four years.

sections.title: Qualifications for Studying Law in the United Kingdom
sections.lead: The university, course level, prior education, and the student's desired professional path all affect eligibility.

items: For Courses for Undergraduates
Completion of Class 12 or a recognized equivalent.
Academic standing that satisfies the prerequisites for admission to the university.
Proficiency with the English language is necessary.
Certain academic backgrounds or subject requirements may be specified by certain universities.
A strong interest in legal studies, communication abilities, and critical thinking may be required of applicants.
For Graduate Programs
A validated bachelor's degree.
A legal degree is often necessary or preferable for a LLM, while some programs allow graduates from other fields.
Academic grades or a comparable classification are necessary.
Proficiency in English that satisfies university criteria.
Certain specialized programs may benefit from relevant work experience.
Regarding Research Initiatives
A master's degree is frequently among the necessary academic credentials.
The chosen study topic is outlined in a research proposal.
When asked, include a CV and academic references.
Proof of subject-matter expertise and research skills.
Proficiency in English, where necessary.

sections.title: UK legal admission requirements
sections.lead: Students need to fulfill the academic, language and application requirements of the university they choose.

items: Academic Qualifications
Usually, an accepted high school diploma with the required grades is needed for admission to undergraduate study.
Postgraduate applications usually require a recognized bachelor's degree.
Some universities may require some qualifications or grades.
Some programs may consider prior legal education or work experience.
Foreign applicants may be required to prove their English language proficiency by means of a recognized exam such as IELTS Academic or other credentials authorized by the university.
Institutions and programs have varying score requirements. Some universities have higher requirements for certain components of language.
Depending on the course, students may be required to submit:
A personal statement
Certificates and academic transcripts.
Academic or professional letters of recommendations.
A CV or resume is required for postgraduate applications.
Writing sample for a particular research or postgraduate program.
PhD applicants must submit a research proposal.
Interview or further assessment as appropriate.
Some universities may require entrance exams or other assessments for some undergraduate programs. Students should check the specific prerequisites for the application year and course of interest.

sections.title: Cost of studying law in the UK
sections.lead: The cost of studying law in the UK depends on the university, the level of the course, the location, and the length of study.

items: Tuition cost approx
For many overseas students, undergraduate LLB courses cost between £15,000 and £30,000 a year.
Postgraduate LLM courses cost between £16,000 and £35,000.
The cost of specialized and research programs will vary depending on the structure of the program, its subject matter and the institution.
Approximate cost of living
Students should anticipate having money for personal expenses, transportation, housing, food and utilities.
Accommodation costs between £500 and £1,200 per month, depending on where you live and how you live.
Food and shopping £150 - £300 per month
Getting around each month is between £50 and £150.
Utilities, phones and personal expenses will be an extra £100-£250 per month.

sections.title: The UK Law Admissions Process
sections.lead: The law admissions process in the UK typically includes the following steps:

items.title: Choose a Law Course of Study
items.desc: Select a LLB, graduate-entry legal degree, LLM or research programme based on your academic background and career goals.

items.title: Research Universities
items.desc: Examine the course modules, specializations, tuition fees, location, admission requirements, and opportunities for practical legal experience.

items.title: Check Eligibility
items.desc: Please verify the program's academic and English language prerequisites.

items.title: Prepare Your Documents
items.desc: Collect references, academic transcripts, certificates, passport details and any required English language test results.

items.title: Submit Your Application
items.desc: Many postgraduate applications will go direct to universities, but most undergraduate applications will be made through UCAS. Please note relevant dates and application process.

items.title: Perform Additional Assessments if Needed
items.desc: Go for an interview, take any entrance exams or provide additional documentation, if requested.

items.title: Receive an Offer
items.desc: The university might give you a conditional or unconditional offer. "Fulfill all requirements by the deadline.

items.title: Funding and Accepting the Offer
items.desc: Accept your offer and pay any deposits required by following the instructions of the university. Look into your financing options, including scholarships.

items.title: Get your CAS
items.desc: Students who satisfy the eligibility criteria will be required to obtain a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) from their licensed student sponsor to be eligible to apply for a UK Student visa.

items.title: Apply for student visa in UK
items.desc: Complete the biometric or identity-verification procedure and submit the visa application, along with any supporting documentation.

items.title: Prepare to leave
items.desc: Be sure to arrange accommodation, travel, registration and any university orientation activities before the course begins.

sections.title: Accreditation in the UK, professional recognition, licensing and law
sections.lead: Law is different to most other academic disciplines in that a legal degree does not automatically qualify you to practise as a solicitor or barrister. The professional qualifications required will depend on the legal jurisdiction and the occupation you are seeking.

items: Important Things to Know About
In England and Wales, the Bar Standards Board (BSB) regulates barristers and the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA) regulates solicitors.

The traditional route for most aspiring solicitors is to obtain a degree or equivalent qualification, pass the Solicitors Qualifying Examination (SQE) complete the required qualifying work experience and satisfy the character and suitability requirements.
To become a barrister, you normally need the necessary academic legal knowledge, vocational bar training, qualifying work-based learning or pupilage and the required authorizations.
In Scotland the legal system and the professional certification pathways for solicitors and advocates are different.
Northern Ireland has separate qualifications for the legal profession.
International recognition If students are planning to work in India or another country, they should check with the local regulator to see if their UK qualification is professionally recognized.

faqs.q: Is studying law in the UK the best choice ?
faqs.a: Yes. The UK offers opportunities to study legal principles, case law and international legal issues, with universities recognized around the world and a wide choice of legal specializations. Students should select a course that is appropriate to their chosen career path and academic interests.

faqs.q: How long does it take to do a law degree in the UK?
faqs.a: In England, Wales and Northern Ireland a LLB is normally a three year full time course. LLM programs take a full year for many. Becoming an attorney or barrister depends on the professional path, necessary training, tests and real-world experience.

faqs.q: What are the qualifications to study law in the UK?
faqs.a: Usually, to apply as an undergraduate, you must have a recognized high school diploma with the necessary marks. Postgraduate applications usually require a recognized bachelor's degree, and an LLM may require a law background. You may also need to submit some extra application documents and have a good command of English.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to study law in the UK?
faqs.a: International undergraduate law tuition can be around £15,000 to £30,000 per year, whilst LLM programs range from £16,000 to £35,000. There are other costs like the cost of living, immigration fees and any professional training or assessment fees.

faqs.q: Can foreign students practice law in the UK after graduation?
faqs.a: International students can follow a law career if they meet the required immigration and professional requirements. The process is different for the legal professions in Scotland and Northern Ireland and for solicitors and barristers in England and Wales. Merely having a law degree does not make a graduate eligible to practice.
